[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance describes how Platform Engineering authors a CI/CD pipeline template for a Golden Path. It covers the required pipeline stages, parameterization approach, verification layer integration, environment progression model, and pre-submission validation required before ARB approval. This guidance implements [PTN-TECH-GOV-001](../../../../patterns/technology/governance/PTN-TECH-GOV-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-template-pattern.md) — the normative specification that defines the required stage composition, PIPE-001 through PIPE-006 conformance checks, and the `workflow-params.yaml` manifest. The steps in this guidance operationalize that specification.

A CI/CD pipeline template is the workflow component of a Golden Path bundle. It is one of five components required for ARB submission. The template is a reusable pipeline definition — authored as a GitHub Actions reusable workflow, an Azure Pipelines `extends` template, or a Jenkins Shared Library — that development teams reference from their service repositories. They do not write their own pipelines. When a team references the Golden Path pipeline template, they inherit the standard build, test, conformance, security scan, and deployment stages that the path requires, without configuring any of them individually.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- Every service on a Golden Path runs the same build, scan, and conformance checks — eliminating per-team pipeline drift
- Conformance Gate (Layer 1) and Fitness Function (Layer 2) checks from the Verification Contract execute automatically on every commit without team configuration
- Compliance evidence (conformance check output, SAST results, dependency scan results) is produced on every build and written to the Compliance Evidence Store
- Teams add business logic; they do not configure pipeline stages, scanner thresholds, or deployment targets

#### Scope Boundaries

- **In Scope**: The reusable CI/CD pipeline template (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, or Jenkins), its required stages, parameterization, verification layer integration, and pre-submission validation
- **Out of Scope**: Infrastructure provisioning (Terraform module); the application scaffold (GUID-APP-IMPL-003); the Verification Contract (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001); configuring the verification tools themselves (covered by PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002) — the pipeline template calls those tools, it does not configure them

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The pipeline template is how the Verification Contract's checks become mandatory rather than optional. A path can specify that "all services must expose a `/health` endpoint," but without a pipeline template that executes `conformance-check --check health-endpoint` on every commit, the check is only run when a team remembers to include it. The pipeline template makes the check non-optional by construction — teams reference the template and the checks run.

For HIPAA and FedRAMP paths, the pipeline also generates the build-level compliance evidence that auditors require. Conformance check results, SAST scan outputs, dependency vulnerability reports, and container image scan results are all produced by the pipeline and written to the Compliance Evidence Store on every build.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Golden Path pipeline templates are reusable pipeline definitions stored at `catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/` in the Golden Path Catalog repository. Teams reference the template from their service repositories using the platform's native template-reference mechanism — they do not copy or modify it, they pass parameters to it.

This guidance is platform-agnostic at the stage and principle level. Platform-specific syntax is isolated to the Key Approaches and Examples sections. The three supported implementation platforms are:

| Platform | Template Mechanism | Consumer Reference | Branch Condition | Credential Model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GitHub Actions** | `on: workflow_call` reusable workflow | `uses: org/repo/.github/workflows/...@vX.Y.Z` | `github.ref` | OIDC via `azure/login` with `use-oidc: true` |
| **Azure Pipelines** | `extends:` YAML template in a central repository | `extends: templates/gp-001-dotnet.yml@gp-catalog` | `Build.SourceBranch` | Federated credentials / workload identity on service connection |
| **Jenkins** | Shared Library (`@Library`) with a `call()` method | `@Library('gp-catalog@v1.0.0')` + `gpPipeline(...)` | `env.BRANCH_NAME` | OIDC credential binding plugin or Azure credentials plugin |

The pipeline template integrates the four verification layers at the appropriate pipeline stages:

- **Layer 1 (Conformance Gate)**: Runs at build time, after compilation, before any artifact is produced. Blocks the pipeline on failure.
- **Layer 2 (Fitness Functions)**: Runs against a deployed test instance in the CI/CD environment. Blocks promotion to staging on failure.
- **Layer 3 (Policy-as-Code)**: Runs against the Terraform plan before any infrastructure is provisioned. Blocks infrastructure provisioning on failure.
- **Layer 4 (Runtime Monitors)**: Not pipeline stages — monitors are provisioned by the `invariant-monitor-provisioner` step at first deployment and run continuously thereafter.

### Current State

The CI/CD pipeline template is the least standardized component of the Golden Path bundle. Most teams have ad-hoc pipeline definitions — in whatever CI/CD tool their product group uses — that vary significantly in stage composition, scanner configuration, and deployment target definition. The pipeline template authoring guidance establishes what a conforming pipeline template must contain and why, regardless of the CI/CD platform.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#principle-1-teams-reference-they-do-not-modify]

#### Principle 1: Teams Reference, They Do Not Modify

**Description:** A service repository references the pipeline template using the platform's native template-reference mechanism (`uses:` in GitHub Actions, `extends:` in Azure Pipelines, `@Library` in Jenkins) and provides the three standard parameters. Teams do not copy pipeline stages into their own definitions.

**Rationale:** A copied pipeline drifts from the template the moment it is copied. Security scanner version updates, new conformance checks, and policy changes applied to the template do not reach copied pipelines. The entire value of a standardized pipeline depends on teams referencing a single maintained version.

**Application:** The template must expose only the parameters teams are expected to vary (`service_name`, `team`, `environment`). All other configuration — scanner thresholds, conformance check flags, registry endpoints, deployment targets — is hardcoded in the template. If a team cannot parameterize what they need, the answer is to update the template through the standard path update process, not to copy and modify.
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#principle-2-every-verification-layer-step-is-non-optional]

#### Principle 2: Every Verification Layer Step Is Non-Optional

**Description:** Every check in the path's Verification Contract that maps to a pipeline stage must be a required step that fails the pipeline on a non-zero exit code. No verification check may be soft-blocked or comment-only on the main branch. Platform syntax: `continue-on-error: false` (GitHub Actions), `continueOnError: false` (Azure Pipelines), `catchError(buildResult: 'FAILURE')` wrapper removed (Jenkins).

**Rationale:** Optional checks are skipped. A conformance gate configured with `continue-on-error: true` is not a gate — it is a notification. The compliance evidence value of the check depends on it being mandatory: a passing check on a mandatory gate is evidence; a passing check on an optional gate is not.

**Application:** Feature branches may use `warn_only` for newly introduced checks (see GUID-GOV-IMPL-001, Principle 4). The main branch always uses `fail`. The template enforces this distinction based on the branch context, not team configuration.
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#principle-3-no-inline-credentials]

#### Principle 3: No Inline Credentials

**Description:** No secret value — registry password, deployment token, API key — appears inline in the pipeline template or as a secret injected by the team. All credentials are retrieved by the pipeline runner using workload identity (OIDC) at runtime.

**Rationale:** Inline secrets are the primary source of CI/CD credential exposure. Workload identity eliminates the credential surface entirely — there is nothing to rotate, nothing to leak, and the pipeline's identity is tied to the runner, not a personal token.

**Application:** Platform-specific credential pattern:
- **GitHub Actions**: `azure/login@v2` with `use-oidc: true`; no `client-secret` input
- **Azure Pipelines**: Azure Resource Manager service connection configured for workload identity federation; no stored password
- **Jenkins**: Azure Credentials Plugin with `azureServicePrincipal` using federated credentials, or OIDC credential binding plugin

In all cases, container registry authentication uses the managed identity of the runner. Teams do not configure any secrets for standard pipeline stages.
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#principle-4-pipeline-version-is-part-of-the-path-version]

#### Principle 4: Pipeline Version Is Part of the Path Version

**Description:** The pipeline template is versioned in sync with the path. When the path publishes version `1.3.0`, the pipeline template version also becomes `1.3.0`. Service repositories pin to a path version, which determines which pipeline template version they run.

**Rationale:** A service on GP-001 `v1.2.0` runs the `v1.2.0` pipeline. A service on GP-001 `v1.3.0` runs the `v1.3.0` pipeline. Version-pinning is what makes it possible to safely introduce new checks: existing adopters are not involuntarily moved to a new check set when a path update is published.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#approach-1-github-actions-reusable-workflow-workflowcall]

#### Approach 1: GitHub Actions Reusable Workflow (`workflow_call`)

**Overview:** The pipeline template is a GitHub Actions reusable workflow (`on: workflow_call`) that exposes inputs matching the three standard Golden Path parameters. Service repositories call it with a single `uses:` job.

**When to Use:** When GitHub Actions is the CI/CD platform.

**Structure:**
```
catalog/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/
├── workflow.yaml          ← Reusable workflow (on: workflow_call)
└── workflow-params.yaml   ← Input parameter schema (mirrors template.yaml parameters)
```

**Consumer reference (in service repo):**
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yaml
jobs:
  pipeline:
    uses: gainwell/gp-catalog/.github/workflows/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/workflow.yaml@v1.0.0
    with:
      service_name: claims-eligibility-api
      team: claims-team
      environment: staging
    secrets: inherit
```
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#approach-2-azure-pipelines-extends-template]

#### Approach 2: Azure Pipelines `extends` Template

**Overview:** The pipeline template is a YAML template file stored in the Golden Path Catalog repository. Service pipelines extend it with `extends:`, providing the three standard parameters. Azure Pipelines enforces that service pipelines may only extend from approved catalog templates (YAML template approval in organization settings).

**When to Use:** When Azure Pipelines (Azure DevOps) is the CI/CD platform.

**Structure:**
```
catalog/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/
├── pipeline-template.yml  ← Azure Pipelines extends template (parameters + stages)
└── workflow-params.yaml   ← Input parameter schema
```

**Consumer reference (in service repo):**
```yaml
# azure-pipelines.yml
resources:
  repositories:
    - repository: gpCatalog
      type: git
      name: gainwell/gp-catalog
      ref: refs/tags/v1.0.0

extends:
  template: catalog/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/pipeline-template.yml@gpCatalog
  parameters:
    serviceName: claims-eligibility-api
    team: claims-team
    environment: staging
```
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#approach-3-jenkins-shared-library]

#### Approach 3: Jenkins Shared Library

**Overview:** The pipeline template is a Groovy `call()` method in a Jenkins Shared Library stored in the Golden Path Catalog repository. Service `Jenkinsfile`s load the library at a pinned tag and call the pipeline function with the three standard parameters. The Shared Library is configured as a "Global Shared Library" in Jenkins, restricting modification to Platform Engineering.

**When to Use:** When Jenkins is the CI/CD platform.

**Structure:**
```
catalog/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/
├── vars/
│   └── gp001DotnetPipeline.groovy   ← Shared Library call() method
└── workflow-params.yaml             ← Input parameter schema
```

**Consumer reference (in service repo):**
```groovy
// Jenkinsfile
@Library('gp-catalog@v1.0.0') _

gp001DotnetPipeline(
  serviceName: 'claims-eligibility-api',
  team: 'claims-team',
  environment: 'staging'
)
```
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#approach-4-composite-injectable-steps]

#### Approach 4: Composite Injectable Steps

**Overview:** For paths where individual pipeline stages must be composed with team-specific steps (for example, a data pipeline path where teams add custom ETL validation between standard stages), the template can be structured as a set of composite actions or shared steps rather than a single reusable call.

**When to Use:** Only when injection points between standard stages are a documented requirement for the path's workload class. Use Approaches 1, 2, or 3 by default.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- **Fail the pipeline at the earliest stage possible.** Conformance Gate (Layer 1) runs before unit tests. If the directory structure is wrong, there is no value in running the full test suite. Ordering: compile → Layer 1 → unit test → SAST → SCA → build image → scan image → Layer 2 → Layer 3 (on terraform) → deploy staging → smoke test → approve → deploy prod → provision monitors → PHI fitness functions (HIPAA paths) → compliance evidence upload.
- **Separate the main-branch and pull-request trigger behaviors.** PRs from feature branches may run newly added checks in `warn_only` mode to allow teams time to remediate. The push-to-main trigger always uses `fail` mode for all checks. Implement with the platform's branch condition: `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` (GitHub Actions), `eq(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/heads/main')` (Azure Pipelines), `env.BRANCH_NAME == 'main'` (Jenkins).
- **Pin all tool versions in the template.** Scanner version `X.Y.Z` produces reproducible results. Scanner version `latest` produces a different result on different days. Every `uses:` and `run:` step in the template references a pinned version. Version bumps go through the standard path update process.
- **Write the compliance evidence output to a standard location.** All scan outputs, conformance check results, and fitness function reports are written to `reports/` in the build workspace and uploaded as job artifacts. The Compliance Evidence Store step retrieves them from this location. Teams do not need to configure evidence collection.
- **Include a `dry-run` input for validation testing.** The template exposes a boolean `dry_run` input. When true, all deployment steps are skipped but all verification steps run. This allows Platform Engineering to validate the template against a test service without affecting any environment.
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Making scanner thresholds configurable by teams.** If a team can set their own CVSS threshold for the dependency vulnerability scan, they can set it to 10.0 (block nothing). Scanner thresholds are path constants in the template — not team inputs.
- **Skipping the image scan step to reduce pipeline time.** Container image scanning (e.g., Trivy) catches vulnerabilities introduced by base image updates that source-level SAST cannot detect. It is a required step on all HIPAA and FedRAMP paths. If pipeline duration is a concern, run it in parallel with unit tests, not after.
- **Using a manual trigger as the primary trigger.** The pipeline must run on every push and pull request automatically. Manual dispatch (`workflow_dispatch` in GitHub Actions, manual run in Azure DevOps, `Build Now` in Jenkins) is an addition, not a replacement.
- **Deploying to production without a gated approval step.** All Golden Path pipeline templates include a mandatory production approval gate that requires at least one human approval before the production deploy job runs. This is not configurable. Platform equivalents: GitHub environment protection rule (`environment: production`), Azure Pipelines deployment environment with approval check, Jenkins `input` step with `submitter` restriction.
- **Authoring the pipeline before the Verification Contract Layer 1 and Layer 2 checks are finalized.** The pipeline calls the check commands defined in the contract. If the contract is not finalized, the pipeline references commands that may change. Author the contract first (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phases 1–3), then author the pipeline.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#required-pipeline-stages]

### Required Pipeline Stages

Every Golden Path pipeline template must implement these stages in this order. Stages marked **mandatory** may not be removed or made optional on the main branch. Stages marked **conditional** apply only to paths with the noted compliance scope.

| Stage | Trigger | Mandatory | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Compile / Build** | all | ✅ | Compile the project. Fail immediately on compile error. |
| **2. Layer 1 — Conformance Gate** | all | ✅ | Run `conformance-check` against the repository. All Layer 1 checks from the Verification Contract must pass. |
| **3. Unit Tests** | all | ✅ | Run the service's unit test suite. Minimum pass rate: 100% (no skipped tests on main). |
| **4. SAST Scan** | all | ✅ | Run static analysis (CodeQL or equivalent). Upload SARIF results to the platform's security findings store (GitHub Advanced Security, Azure DevOps Advanced Security, or a Jenkins SARIF plugin) and to the Compliance Evidence Store. |
| **5. SCA — Dependency Vulnerability Scan** | all | ✅ | Run dependency vulnerability scan (OWASP Dependency-Check or Snyk). Fail on CVSS ≥ 7.0 for production branches. |
| **6. Build Artifact** | push | ✅ | Build and package the path's deployable artifact. Artifact type, build tool, and base image or base package are path constants — not team inputs. Tag includes commit SHA and path version. (e.g., container image, npm bundle, Python wheel, NuGet package) |
| **7. Artifact Security Scan** | push | ✅ | Run a security scan appropriate to the artifact type. Fail threshold is a path constant. Output written to `reports/artifact-scan.json`. (e.g., Trivy for container images; Snyk or `npm audit` for npm bundles; `safety` for Python wheels) |
| **8. Publish to Approved Artifact Store** | push to main | ✅ | Publish to the approved artifact management endpoint for the path's workload class using OIDC workload identity. Endpoint is a path constant declared in `workflow-params.yaml`. Do not publish to public artifact stores. |
| **9. Layer 2 — Fitness Functions** | push to main | ✅ | Deploy to CI test environment. Run `fitness-function-runner` against the deployed service. All Layer 2 checks from the Verification Contract must pass. |
| **10. Layer 3 — Policy-as-Code** | push to main | ✅ (infra paths) | Run `opa eval` against Terraform plan. All Layer 3 checks from the Verification Contract must pass before `terraform apply`. |
| **11. Deploy to Staging** | push to main | ✅ | Deploy to staging environment using workload identity. No manual credential injection. |
| **12. Staging Smoke Test** | push to main | ✅ | Call `GET /health` and `GET /info` on the deployed staging instance. Both must return HTTP 200. |
| **13. Production Approval Gate** | push to main | ✅ | Mandatory human approval before production deploy. Minimum 1 approval from `platform-leads`. Platform: GitHub environment protection rule; Azure Pipelines deployment environment approval; Jenkins `input` step with restricted submitter. |
| **14. Deploy to Production** | after approval | ✅ | Deploy to production environment using workload identity. |
| **15. Layer 4 — Monitor Provisioning** | first production deploy | ✅ | Run `invariant-monitor-provisioner --contract {path-id}-verification-contract.yaml`. Activates runtime monitors for this deployment. |
| **16. PHI Fitness Functions** | push to main | ✅ (HIPAA paths) | Additional fitness function run exercising PHI-bearing requests. PHI string must not appear in log output (FF-001). |
| **17. Compliance Evidence Upload** | all | ✅ | Upload all scan outputs and check results to Compliance Evidence Store with build ID, commit SHA, and path version metadata. |
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#authoring-workflow-overview]

### Authoring Workflow Overview

```
Phase 1: Prerequisites
    → Verification Contract Layer 1 and Layer 2 checks finalized (GUID-GOV-IMPL-001 Phases 1–3)
    → Scaffold template authored (GUID-APP-IMPL-003)
    → Approved container registry endpoint confirmed
    → Workload identity (OIDC) configured for CI/CD runner in target environments

Phase 2: Pipeline Skeleton
    → Create the platform template file in catalog/ci-cd/{path-id}/:
        GitHub Actions:   workflow.yaml  (on: workflow_call)
        Azure Pipelines:  pipeline-template.yml  (parameters: + stages:)
        Jenkins:          vars/gp###Pipeline.groovy  (def call(Map params))
    → Create workflow-params.yaml at the template root — this is the machine-readable manifest for ARB review;
      it declares the path ID, platform, all 17 required stages (or documents omissions with rationale),
      the check IDs wired at each stage, the compliance scope (hipaa/fedramp/none), and
      the PIPE check IDs (PIPE-001 through PIPE-006) that will be validated at pre-submission.
      See PTN-TECH-GOV-001 §Solution for the full field specification.
    → Define inputs/parameters: service_name, team, environment, dry_run (boolean, default: false)
    → Add all 17 required stages as empty jobs/stages/steps with correct sequential dependencies
    → Confirm template is syntactically valid:
        GitHub Actions:   gh workflow lint
        Azure Pipelines:  az pipelines validate (or PR dry-run)
        Jenkins:          Replay from Jenkins UI against a test branch

Phase 3: Build and Static Analysis Stages (Stages 1–5)
    → Wire Stage 1 (compile) with appropriate build command for the path's language stack
    → Wire Stage 2 (conformance-check) using check IDs from Verification Contract Layer 1 section
    → Wire stages 3–5 with pinned tool versions
    → Validate: run against scaffold-instantiated test service; all stages must pass

Phase 4: Artifact Build, Scan, and Publish Stages (Stages 6–8)
    → Wire Stage 6 (Build Artifact) using the build tool and artifact type for the path's workload class;
      build tool, base image/package, and runtime version are path constants in workflow-params.yaml
    → Wire Stage 7 (Artifact Security Scan) with a pinned tool version appropriate to the artifact type;
      fail severity threshold is a path constant; output written to reports/artifact-scan.json
    → Wire Stage 8 (Publish to Approved Artifact Store) using OIDC workload identity;
      the artifact_store endpoint is a path constant from workflow-params.yaml; no team-injectable credentials
    → Validate: artifact is published at the expected tag/version in the approved artifact management system

Phase 5: Deployment and Verification Stages (Stages 9–15)
    → Wire fitness function runner (Stage 9) using check IDs from Verification Contract Layer 2 section
    → Wire OPA eval (Stage 10) for infrastructure paths
    → Wire staging deploy and smoke test (Stages 11–12)
    → Configure GitHub environment protection rule for production (Stage 13)
    → Wire production deploy (Stage 14)
    → Wire invariant-monitor-provisioner (Stage 15)

Phase 6: Compliance Evidence and Path-Specific Stages (Stages 16–17)
    → Wire PHI fitness functions for HIPAA-scoped paths (Stage 16)
    → Wire compliance evidence upload step (Stage 17) with correct metadata fields
    → Confirm evidence is queryable in Compliance Evidence Store after test run

Phase 7: Validation and ARB Submission
    → Run full pipeline against scaffold-instantiated test service (dry_run: false)
    → All 17 stages must pass
    → Confirm compliance evidence record created in Compliance Evidence Store
    → Include workflow.yaml and validation run ID in ARB submission package
```

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#pre-submission-checklist]

### Pre-Submission Checklist

| Item | PIPE Check | Check |
|---|---|---|
| All 17 required stages present and ordered correctly; any omission documented in `workflow-params.yaml` with rationale | PIPE-001 | ☐ |

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#decision-point-1-when-should-a-stage-fail-vs-warn-on-a-pull-request-branch]

#### Decision Point 1: When Should a Stage Fail vs Warn on a Pull Request Branch?

**Context:** A new check is being added to the Verification Contract. Existing service repositories are on an older path version where the check did not exist. A team opens a PR that fails the new check.

**Options:**
- Hard fail on all branches immediately
- Warn on feature branches, hard fail on main

**Recommendation:** Warn on feature branches, hard fail on main. This is implemented by checking `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` in the stage condition. New checks on new path versions should be introduced in `warn_only` mode on feature branches for one path release cycle to allow teams time to remediate before the check fails their PRs. On main, `warn_only` is never appropriate after the check is finalized.
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#decision-point-2-hipaa-path--run-phi-fitness-functions-on-every-pr]

#### Decision Point 2: HIPAA Path — Run PHI Fitness Functions on Every PR?

**Context:** PHI fitness functions (Stage 16) require deploying the service to the CI test environment and sending synthetic PHI-bearing requests. This adds pipeline time.

**Options:**
- Run on every push (PR branches + main)
- Run on main branch only

**Recommendation:** Run on main and on any PR targeting main. Skip on feature-to-feature-branch PRs. PHI fitness functions are compliance evidence and must run before any merge to the main branch. Use a `paths:` filter to also trigger on changes to logging configuration, serialization code, or `.ai/context.yaml` regardless of target branch.
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#decision-point-3-what-if-the-path-has-no-infrastructure-component]

#### Decision Point 3: What If the Path Has No Infrastructure Component?

**Context:** The path is for a front-end micro-frontend module. It has no Terraform module and no Kubernetes deployment manifest. Stage 10 (Layer 3 Policy-as-Code) is not applicable.

**Options:**
- Include the stage as a no-op
- Remove the stage

**Recommendation:** Remove the stage and document the omission in `workflow-params.yaml` with `stage_10_policy_as_code: not_applicable` and a rationale. Do not include a no-op stage — no-op stages appear as passing steps in compliance evidence, which is misleading. Absence is explicit; a false pass is not.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#example-1-gp-001-pipeline-template-structure-condensed]

### Example 1: GP-001 Pipeline Template Structure (Condensed)

```yaml
# catalog/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/workflow.yaml
name: GP-001 HIPAA REST Microservice Pipeline

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      service_name:
        required: true
        type: string
      team:
        required: true
        type: string
      environment:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: staging
      dry_run:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.x'        # Path constant — not a team input
      - run: dotnet build --configuration Release

  conformance-gate:
    name: Layer 1 — Conformance Gate
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: |
          conformance-check \
            --path-id GP-001 \
            --contract catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-verification-contract.yaml \
            --checks layer1 \
            --output reports/conformance-layer1.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: conformance-layer1
          path: reports/conformance-layer1.json

  unit-tests:
    name: Unit Tests
    needs: conformance-gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: dotnet test --logger trx --results-directory reports/

  # ... sast, sca, image-build, image-scan, registry-push (Stages 4–8) ...

  fitness-functions:
    name: Layer 2 — Fitness Functions
    needs: [registry-push]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Deploy to CI test environment
        run: |
          kubectl apply -f k8s/ \
            --namespace ci-${{ inputs.service_name }} \
            --wait
      - name: Run fitness functions
        run: |
          fitness-function-runner \
            --path-id GP-001 \
            --contract catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-verification-contract.yaml \
            --checks layer2 \
            --target https://${{ inputs.service_name }}.ci.internal \
            --output reports/fitness-functions.json

  phi-fitness-functions:
    name: Layer 2 — PHI Fitness Functions (HIPAA)
    needs: [fitness-functions]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Run PHI-bearing request and verify no PHI in logs
        run: |
          fitness-function-runner \
            --path-id GP-001 \
            --checks phi \
            --target https://${{ inputs.service_name }}.ci.internal \
            --output reports/phi-fitness.json

  deploy-staging:
    name: Deploy to Staging
    needs: [phi-fitness-functions]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !inputs.dry_run
    environment: staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
          use-oidc: true          # PIPE-003: OIDC workload identity — no client secret injected
      - run: |
          az aks get-credentials --resource-group rg-staging --name aks-staging
          helm upgrade --install ${{ inputs.service_name }} \
            catalog/helm/${{ inputs.service_name }} \
            --set image.tag=${{ github.sha }}

  production-approval:
    name: Production Approval Gate
    needs: [deploy-staging]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && !inputs.dry_run
    environment:
      name: production      # GitHub environment protection rule: requires 1 approval from platform-leads
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Approved for production deployment"

  deploy-production:
    name: Deploy to Production
    needs: [production-approval]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID_PROD }}
          tenant-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID_PROD }}
          use-oidc: true          # PIPE-003: OIDC workload identity — no client secret injected
      - run: |
          az aks get-credentials --resource-group rg-production --name aks-production
          helm upgrade --install ${{ inputs.service_name }} \
            catalog/helm/${{ inputs.service_name }} \
            --set image.tag=${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Provision Layer 4 runtime monitors
        run: |
          invariant-monitor-provisioner \
            --contract catalog/verification-contracts/GP-001-verification-contract.yaml \
            --service ${{ inputs.service_name }} \
            --namespace production

  compliance-evidence:
    name: Upload Compliance Evidence
    needs: [deploy-production]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Upload to Compliance Evidence Store
        run: |
          evidence-uploader \
            --build-id ${{ github.run_id }} \
            --commit-sha ${{ github.sha }} \
            --path-id GP-001 \
            --path-version 1.0.0 \
            --service ${{ inputs.service_name }} \
            --reports-dir reports/
```

### Example 2: Team Reference From Service Repository

**GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`):
```yaml
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'feature/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  pipeline:
    uses: gainwell/gp-catalog/.github/workflows/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/workflow.yaml@v1.0.0
    with:
      service_name: claims-eligibility-api
      team: claims-team
      environment: staging
    secrets: inherit
```

**Azure Pipelines** (`azure-pipelines.yml`):
```yaml
resources:
  repositories:
    - repository: gpCatalog
      type: git
      name: gainwell/gp-catalog
      ref: refs/tags/v1.0.0

trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main, feature/*]
pr:
  branches:
    include: [main]

extends:
  template: catalog/ci-cd/gp-001-dotnet/pipeline-template.yml@gpCatalog
  parameters:
    serviceName: claims-eligibility-api
    team: claims-team
    environment: staging
```

**Jenkins** (`Jenkinsfile`):
```groovy
@Library('gp-catalog@v1.0.0') _

gp001DotnetPipeline(
  serviceName: 'claims-eligibility-api',
  team: 'claims-team',
  environment: 'staging'
)
```

In all three cases the team writes fewer than 15 lines. They receive all 17 pipeline stages, all conformance checks, all compliance evidence collection, and the production approval gate. They do not configure any of it.

### Use Case Scenario: New Compliance Requirement Propagates to All Adopters

A regulatory change requires GP-001 services to enforce TLS 1.3 minimum on all ingress connections. Platform Engineering updates:
1. The path's `constraints.md` (new rule)
2. The Verification Contract (new Layer 3 check `OPA-003`)
3. The OPA policy bundle (new Rego rule)
4. The pipeline template (Stage 10 now includes `OPA-003` in its check set)
5. Publishes GP-001 `v1.3.0`

All service repositories referencing `@v1.3.0` automatically run the new check on their next pipeline execution. Services that fail `OPA-003` receive a pipeline failure with the exact policy that failed. Platform Engineering updates the Kubernetes ingress configuration in the Terraform module. Teams merge the catalog version updater PR to their `v1.3.0` migration branch and the check passes.

No team needed to discover the new requirement independently, author a check, or update their own pipeline.

### Standards Alignment

The pipeline template is the execution layer for the Verification Contract. Every check declared in the contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003) must have a corresponding pipeline stage executing the check command. The template version and contract version must remain synchronized.

For HIPAA paths, the pipeline generates compliance evidence required to substantiate the following controls:
- **§ 164.312(a)(2)(iv)** — Encryption: covered by Trivy image scan and OPA infrastructure checks
- **§ 164.312(b)** — Audit controls: covered by PHI fitness functions and Layer 4 audit event monitors
- **§ 164.312(c)(1)** — Integrity: covered by conformance gate structural checks and image digest pinning

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-001-golden-path-cicd-pipeline-authoring-guidance.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

The pipeline template is submitted as part of the complete Golden Path bundle ARB submission. The ARB will not approve a path without a pipeline template that passes a full end-to-end dry-run validation. Minor pipeline updates (tool version bumps, adding a new optional stage for a new language variant) may follow the minor update process (PTN-GOV-AI-001). Changes to required stage composition, check IDs, or environment progression model require ARB review.
